findings.description: Degraded/absent-rate fallback: the real code (`eff_rate.map(fmt_ppm).unwrap_or_default()`) writes the Est. Tax Rate cell as the literal empty string `""` when a symbol is absent from `effective_rates` — never `0%`, never a blank/omitted CellData, never an error token — so Sheets coerces the referencing `=G*H`/`=G*(1-H)` cells to 0 in arithmetic. SHEET-FORMULA-005's text says nothing about the absent/degraded case at all (it only covers the present-rate numeric-parsing property). This is the strongest finding because it triangulates cleanly: B1/B2/B3 unanimously extract this exact empty-string behavior from the code, while the three A-sketches — reading the same spec text blind to the code — independently invent three DIFFERENT, mutually incompatible fallbacks (A1: `0.0` numeric with a PERCENT format; A2: an entirely blank `CellData::default()`; A3: the string `"0.00%"`). None of the three A-runs converges on, or guesses, the real behavior, which is exactly what you'd expect when a requirement is genuinely silent on a case the code nonetheless pins.

Exact precision/normalization constant: `fmt_ppm` fixes the decomposition as `whole = |ppm| / 10_000`, `frac = |ppm| % 10_000` zero-padded to exactly 4 digits (e.g. `Ppm(150_000)` → `"15.0000%"`). This 4-decimal-digit convention is a hardcoded source-level constant (not literally asserted by a test, but load-bearing and unanimous across B1/B2/B3's reconstructions) that SHEET-FORMULA-005 never states — the spec only requires 'parses as a number,' not any particular display precision. All three A-sketches instead invented a 2-decimal `"0.00%"` pattern, confirming the precision is pure code-side surplus with no spec anchor in either direction.

Row-anchored, no-cross-row-leakage contract on the per-row live formulas: the code builds `Market Value`, `Unrealized P&L` (and, by the same `cell_ref(_, r)` construction, `Est. Unrealized Tax = G{r}*H{r}` / `Net Unrealized = G{r}*(1-H{r})`) referencing only row r's own cells, and the test `per_row_formulas_reference_their_own_row_beneath_frozen_header` explicitly regression-checks every row's Market Value/Unrealized P&L formula against every OTHER row's cell refs to rule out leakage. SHEET-FORMULA-005's text is scoped narrowly to the Est. Tax Rate cell's numeric typing and says nothing about this row-anchoring/anti-leak property of the consuming formulas. B1/B2/B3 unanimously surface it (though note: the anti-leak test itself only exercises Market Value/Unrealized P&L across multiple rows, not Est. Unrealized Tax/Net Unrealized specifically — B1-3's claim that this is 'verified per-row' for the post-tax columns too is a slight overreach beyond what the cited test actually checks, even though it's true of the code's construction).

Softer/tempered finding — mechanism ambiguity, not a hard spec-vs-code gap: the EARS text's own example ('e.g. a `%`-suffixed value') most literally maps to writing a percent-suffixed STRING and relying on Sheets' typed-entry auto-parse via `userEnteredValue` — which is exactly what the real `fmt_ppm`+`Cell::Value`+`batch_update_view` contract does, and what A3 alone reconstructs. A1 and A2 (2 of 3 runs) instead invent a structurally different mechanism — a raw `numberValue` fraction plus an explicit `numberFormat: PERCENT` — explicitly reasoning that a string value would NOT be reparsed by the Sheets API, which contradicts the real client's documented contract ('a `Cell::Value` is written as a Sheets `userEnteredValue`... so Sheets parses it the way a human typing the same text would... a percent-suffixed string... as the numeric fraction'). This is real A-direction instability on a load-bearing representational choice — not counted as a strict 'spec states X, code lacks X' finding, since the code's actual outcome (numeric parsing) is preserved under either mechanism, but worth flagging as evidence the spec's own example is read inconsistently even by careful implementers, with the majority (2/3) landing on a scheme that diverges from both the literal spec text and the real implementation.

notes:
Core requirement check: the real code DOES satisfy SHEET-FORMULA-005 as literally stated — Est. Tax Rate is written as Cell::Value (never Cell::Formula), the doc contract requires it go through Sheets as `userEnteredValue` (not a forced string/stringValue) precisely so a percent-suffixed literal like \"15.0000%\" parses as the numeric fraction 0.20-style value under a percent format, and the pinned test (`est_tax_rate_cell_is_numeric_percent_the_posttax_formulas_can_multiply`) exercises exactly that property end-to-end. So Direction A does not surface a clean 'spec forces X, code lacks X' gap on the core requirement — the classification rests on Direction B surfacing multiple concrete, code/test-pinned specifics (degraded-value fallback, exact precision, row-anchoring/anti-leak structure) that SHEET-FORMULA-005's text never states, while Direction A's disagreements are either unanimous-and-therefore-excluded assumption artifacts (the Bps/basis-points rate-type invented by all three vs. the real `Ppm` type; the 2-decimal display convention) or non-unanimous mechanism noise that doesn't rise to a hard requirement gap.

Excluded as assumption artifacts per protocol (unanimous A-side, no spec basis): all three A-runs invent a `Bps`/basis-points integer rate type mirroring the Cents convention, versus the real code's `Ppm` (parts-per-million) type from the `config` crate; all three also invent 2-decimal display precision. Neither is stated by the EARS text, so per the classification rubric these are not counted as findings even though they diverge from the real code.

One reconstruction-accuracy nuance (not a spec/code drift, just a B-direction calibration note): B1/B2/B3 all cite the identity `G*H + G*(1-H) == G` as a 'pinned invariant,' but this holds algebraically for ANY value of H (rate need not even be in [0,1] for the identity to hold) — it's a tautology of the two formula shapes, not an independently enforced constraint distinct from finding #3 (the formula-structure finding). Flagging it is accurate but adds no separate signal.

Direction A stability is 'medium' rather than 'low' or 'high': A1/A2 cluster tightly on the primary write mechanism (numberValue+PercentFormat, Bps type, 2-decimal pattern) while A3 diverges on both value representation (string vs. number) and API surface (values.update/USER_ENTERED vs. CellData/batchUpdate) — but all three give three DIFFERENT answers on the degraded/absent-rate fallback, so agreement is partial and axis-dependent, not scattered enough to call 'low' or convergent enough to call 'high.'
